## What I Wanted to Change

I started with Quarto's Cosmo theme and added teal links, a navy navigation
bar, and a light background. I also made a note style and a small project
card. You can see both examples on this page.

HTML gives a page its structure. CSS controls how it looks, including the
colors, fonts, borders, and spacing. SCSS lets me use variables and nest
related rules. Quarto turns that SCSS into CSS when I render the site.

## Load the Style Files

These settings in `_quarto.yml` apply to the regular website pages:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, site.scss]
    css: styles.css
```

`site.scss` changes the theme. `styles.css` adds a few rules for particular
parts of the page. The dashboard loads `dashboard.scss` in its own header
because it has a different layout.

## Try a CSS Class

This note uses `.sample-note` from `styles.css`:

::: {.sample-note}
**Check the scale.** A high borrowing-rate score means the respondent
thinks the rate is high. It doesn't mean they're more satisfied.
:::

```css
.sample-note {
  padding: 1rem 1.25rem;
  margin: 1rem 0;
  border-left: 4px solid #087f8c;
  background-color: #edf4f5;
  color: #183f52;
}
```

`padding` adds space inside the border. `margin` adds space outside it.
The colored border helps the note stand out without making the text bigger.

I attach the class to a Markdown div like this:

```markdown
::: {.sample-note}
The note goes here.
:::
```

## Pick the Right Selector

| Selector | What it selects |
|---|---|
| `h2` | All level-two headings |
| `.sample-note` | Anything with the `sample-note` class |
| `#project-example` | The element with that one ID |
| `.learning-card h3` | Level-three headings inside a learning card |
| `.project-link:hover` | A project link while the pointer is over it |

A class is useful when I want to reuse a style. An ID identifies one
element and can also give me a place to link to on the page.

## Keep Colors in SCSS Variables

I put these variables in the defaults section of `site.scss`:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$portfolio-teal: #087f8c;
$portfolio-navy: #183f52;

$primary: $portfolio-teal;
$navbar-bg: $portfolio-navy;
$navbar-fg: #ffffff;
```

If I want to try another main color, I can change `$portfolio-teal` in one
place. The theme settings and rules using it will use the new value.

## Nest a Rule Inside a Card

::: {#project-example .learning-card}
### My Case 31 dashboard

See the employee ratings and service-awareness charts from the credit union case.

[Open the dashboard](dashboard.qmd){.project-link}
:::

Here's part of the SCSS for that card:

```scss
/*-- scss:rules --*/
.learning-card {
  border: 1px solid #c7d9dd;
  border-top: 4px solid $portfolio-teal;
  border-radius: 0.6rem;
  padding: 1.25rem;

  h3 {
    margin-top: 0;
    color: $portfolio-navy;
  }
}
```

The nested `h3` rule changes headings inside the card. It becomes
`.learning-card h3` in the CSS, so other headings keep their usual style.

## Make Links Easy to Find

The card link has an underline. Its color changes on hover and when it
gets keyboard focus. In `site.scss`, I used this nested rule:

```scss
.project-link {
  color: $portfolio-navy;
  text-decoration: underline;

  &:hover,
  &:focus-visible {
    color: #066773;
    text-decoration-thickness: 0.15em;
  }
}
```

The `&` stands for `.project-link`. I can press Tab to check the focus
style, then narrow the browser window to check how the page fits.
